title: Baidu Open Sources New OCR Tool That Parses Entire Books in Single Requests
summary:
The Chinese technology firm released Unlimited OCR 2, an open source model designed to parse documents of virtually any length while maintaining a stable memory footprint. The tool can handle large files within a finite context window, ensuring that per-step decoding latency remains nearly constant as the document size increases.

The model uses a SR-SWA mechanism to condense attention interactions into working references and recorded state-of-the-art performance on the MarathonDocBench and MPDocBench benchmarks. SGLang, the recommended serving path for the project, stated that the model can process a whole book in a single request with flat memory usage across hundreds of pages.

selectedTweets.text:
Unlimited OCR 2 is here, and it's open source. 📖 ✨

Longer documents can mean a lot more attention computation. Our new SR-SWA mechanism keeps that in check by condensing text-visual attention interactions into a fixed-size set of working references.

Here's what it delivers:
- Document parsing at virtually any length, within a finite context window
- Nearly constant per-step decoding latency and memory footprint as documents grow longer
- State-of-the-art performance on MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench, covering documents from dozens to hundreds of pages
